title: Tourist Problem
statementMd:
Iahub is a big fan of tourists. He wants to become a tourist himself, so he planned a trip. There are $*n*$ destinations on a straight road that Iahub wants to visit. Iahub starts the excursion from kilometer 0. The $*n*$ destinations are described by a non-negative integers sequence $*a*_{1}$, $*a*_{2}$, ..., $*a*_{*n*}$. The number $*a*_{*k*}$ represents that the $*k*$th destination is at distance $*a*_{*k*}$ kilometers from the starting point. No two destinations are located in the same place.

Iahub wants to visit each destination only once. Note that, crossing through a destination is not considered visiting, unless Iahub explicitly wants to visit it at that point. Also, after Iahub visits his last destination, he doesn't come back to kilometer 0, as he stops his trip at the last destination.

The distance between destination located at kilometer $*x*$ and next destination, located at kilometer $*y*$, is $|*x* - *y*|$ kilometers. We call a "route" an order of visiting the destinations. Iahub can visit destinations in any order he wants, as long as he visits all $*n*$ destinations and he doesn't visit a destination more than once.

Iahub starts writing out on a paper all possible routes and for each of them, he notes the total distance he would walk. He's interested in the average number of kilometers he would walk by choosing a route. As he got bored of writing out all the routes, he asks you to help him.

## Input

The first line contains integer $*n*$ ($2 ≤ *n* ≤ 10^{5}$). Next line contains $*n*$ distinct integers $*a*_{1}$, $*a*_{2}$, ..., $*a*_{*n*}$ ($1 ≤ *a*_{*i*} ≤ 10^{7}$).

## Output

Output two integers — the numerator and denominator of a fraction which is equal to the wanted average number. The fraction must be irreducible.

## Note

Consider 6 possible routes:

- [2, 3, 5]: total distance traveled: |2 – 0| + |3 – 2| + |5 – 3| = 5;
- [2, 5, 3]: |2 – 0| + |5 – 2| + |3 – 5| = 7;
- [3, 2, 5]: |3 – 0| + |2 – 3| + |5 – 2| = 7;
- [3, 5, 2]: |3 – 0| + |5 – 3| + |2 – 5| = 8;
- [5, 2, 3]: |5 – 0| + |2 – 5| + |3 – 2| = 9;
- [5, 3, 2]: |5 – 0| + |3 – 5| + |2 – 3| = 8.

The average travel distance is ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/29119d3733c79f70eb2d77186ac1606bf938508a.png) = ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/ee9d5516ed2ca1d2b65ed21f8a64f58f94954c30.png) = ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/ed5cc8cb7dd43cfb27f2459586062538e44de7bd.png).
statementZhMd:
Iahub 是游客的狂热粉丝。他想亲自成为一名游客，因此计划了一次旅行。有一条笔直的道路，路上有 $*n*$ 个 Iahub 想要参观的目的地。Iahub 从公里数 0 处开始这次旅行。这 $*n*$ 个目的地由一个非负整数序列 $*a*_{1}$、$*a*_{2}$、...、$*a*_{*n*}$ 描述。数值 $*a*_{*k*}$ 表示第 $*k*$ 个目的地距离起点 $*a*_{*k*}$ 公里。任意两个目的地都不在同一位置。

Iahub 希望每个目的地只参观一次。注意，经过某个目的地不算参观，除非 Iahub 明确决定在经过该处时参观它。此外，在参观完最后一个目的地后，他不会返回公里数 0 处，而是将旅行终点设在最后一个目的地。

位于公里数 $*x*$ 处的目的地与下一个位于公里数 $*y*$ 处的目的地之间的距离为 $|*x* - *y*|$ 公里。我们将参观各个目的地的顺序称为一条“路线”。只要参观所有 $*n*$ 个目的地且不重复参观任何目的地，Iahub 就可以按照任意顺序参观。

Iahub 开始在纸上写下所有可能的路线，并记录每条路线中他将行走的总距离。他想知道选择一条路线时所行走公里数的平均值。由于写下所有路线让他感到厌烦，所以他请你帮助他。

## 输入格式

第一行包含一个整数 $*n*$（$2 ≤ *n* ≤ 10^{5}$）。

第二行包含 $*n*$ 个互不相同的整数 $*a*_{1}$、$*a*_{2}$、...、$*a*_{*n*}$（$1 ≤ *a*_{*i*} ≤ 10^{7}$）。

## 输出格式

输出两个整数——一个分数的分子和分母，该分数等于所求的平均值。该分数必须是最简分数。

## 说明

考虑以下 6 条可能的路线：

- [2, 3, 5]：行走的总距离为 |2 – 0| + |3 – 2| + |5 – 3| = 5；
- [2, 5, 3]：|2 – 0| + |5 – 2| + |3 – 5| = 7；
- [3, 2, 5]：|3 – 0| + |2 – 3| + |5 – 2| = 7；
- [3, 5, 2]：|3 – 0| + |5 – 3| + |2 – 5| = 8；
- [5, 2, 3]：|5 – 0| + |2 – 5| + |3 – 2| = 9；
- [5, 3, 2]：|5 – 0| + |3 – 5| + |2 – 3| = 8。

平均行走距离为 ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/29119d3733c79f70eb2d77186ac1606bf938508a.png) = ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/ee9d5516ed2ca1d2b65ed21f8a64f58f94954c30.png) = ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/ed5cc8cb7dd43cfb27f2459586062538e44de7bd.png)。
